answer.evidence: The image is a full 96x96 tile of dirt with an L-shaped asphalt road, all seen from straight above. The asphalt is mottled grey over rows 18-77. Its only south edge is a thin dark brown ledge at rows 76-78, 1-2 rows tall. That is a ledge shadow, not a vertical front face of 3+ rows. No eave, no front-edge line and no side face is drawn. The surface is a flat plate with no front face, which suits a flat ground decal.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate has 5 visible tones per tile, above the grass reference (3) and below the paving reference (7). Near-flat coverage is 1%, so there are no flat fills. Only 3% of its dark edge pixels are neutral, so the edges lean brown or grey with the material rather than being a black sticker line. The dirt carries speckle and grain in a few browns, with darker flecks and pebble clusters. The asphalt has a lighter chipped edge and crumb dots, plus a darker ledge on the south side. The ramps are a bit shallow: about 4 steps per material against 5-6 in Beodeul, and only 9 distinct colours in total. The texture is therefore 'some' rather than rich. Per-tile density is still at or above the grass ground reference and not clearly thinner than the paving, so it would sit acceptably next to them.
